newsitem.title: USA: California quake agency 'is open for business' - CEO.
newsitem.headline: California quake agency 'is open for business' - CEO.

text.p: The California Earthquake Authority (CEA) said on Monday it was now operational and would immediately begin selling quake-insurance policies in the state.

After more than a year of wrangling between lawmakers, insurers and consumer groups, the new state authority began operations Monday morning as anticipated, said Greg Butler, the CEA's interim chief executive officer.
"The CEA is open for business," Butler said.
The privately financed, publicly managed agency was proposed after the 1994 Northridge earthquake, which prompted many insurers to bow out of the California market.
The CEA was designed to end the shortage of earthquake insurance in the state and reinvigorate the market for homeowners' coverage, state officials said.

In its first month of operation, the authority was expected to issue about 10,000 earthquake insurance policies. Once fully operational, Butler said the authority could handle up to 1.7 million earthquake policies.
The authority's insurance policies will be written and serviced by private insurers, but the CEA will issue the policy, pay earthquake claims and assume much of the risk.

The CEA will be financed with premiums paid by those who buy earthquake coverage, cash from participating insurance companies, commitments from participating insurers and reinsurance, which insurers use to reduce their risks.
The authority has secured about $3.5 billion of reinsurance and was expected to purchase about $2.5 billion of that amount.
If successful, the authority could become a prototype for similar agencies in other states, experts said.
